name: Pasta Bolognese
reason: Include the milk and cooking oil used in the method and define the dry pasta and meat weights.
steps: Dice the onion, carrot and celery. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan and soften the vegetables for 8 minutes.
Add the beef mince and cook for 5 minutes, breaking it up. Add the wine and simmer for 2–3 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, milk, salt and pepper. Simmer gently for 30–40 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding a little water if needed.
Cook the spaghetti according to its packet instructions. Drain, reserving a little cooking water.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce, loosening with reserved water if needed. Divide into 3 portions and top with the grated Parmesan.

name: Dal
reason: Include tempering oil and cooking water; define dry lentil quantities.
steps: Rinse the lentils. Place in a saucepan with the water and turmeric. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 20 minutes, until soft.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a frying pan. Add the cumin and mustard seeds and cook until fragrant. Add diced onion and cook for 8 minutes.
Add finely chopped garlic and ginger, then the canned tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes.
Stir the tomato mixture into the lentils and simmer for 5–10 minutes. Add water if needed for a spoonable consistency.
Stir in the lemon juice and salt. Divide into 3 portions. Extra rice or bread is optional and is not included in these quantities.

name: Palak Paneer
reason: Include cooking oil and specify the cream and paneer portions.
steps: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, drain and blend to a purée.
Cut the paneer into cubes. Heat the oil in a pan and lightly brown the paneer. Transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, soften diced onion for 8 minutes. Add chopped garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and garam masala and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the spinach, cream and salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the paneer and heat through. Divide into 3 portions. Extra rice or bread is optional and is not included in the quantities.

name: Shakshuka
reason: Define four eggs for two portions, include oil and retain vegetarian-compatible feta.
steps: Dice the onion and pepper. Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the vegetables for 7 minutes.
Add chopped garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 10 minutes.
Make 4 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each one. Cover and cook for 5–7 minutes, until the whites are set; cook longer for firm yolks.
Crumble over the feta and chopped parsley. Divide into 2 portions. Extra bread is optional and is not included in the quantities.

name: Grilled Salmon
reason: Align the title with the pan-searing method and include basting butter and garlic.
steps: Pat the salmon dry and season with the measured salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Place the salmon skin-side down and cook for 4–5 minutes.
Turn the fillets and add the butter, lightly crushed garlic and rosemary. Baste for 2–3 minutes, or until cooked through.
Discard the rosemary stems. Finish with lemon juice and divide between 2 plates. Side dishes are not included in these quantities.

name: Brudet
reason: Specify boneless fish and include the polenta cooking liquid and butter.
ingredients: for polenta; adjust to packet instructions
2 g for stew; 2 g for polenta
steps: Dice the onion. Heat the olive oil in a wide pot and cook the onion for 8 minutes. Add chopped garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the canned tomatoes, vinegar, 2 g salt and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Cut the fish into large pieces and add to the sauce. Cover and simmer gently for 10–15 minutes, until cooked through; shake the pot instead of stirring vigorously.
Meanwhile, bring the water and remaining 2 g salt to a boil. Whisk in the polenta and cook according to its packet instructions, adding water if necessary. Stir in the butter.
Divide the polenta and fish stew into 4 portions and scatter with parsley.
description: Dalmatian-style tomato and white fish stew served over buttery polenta.

name: Samsa
reason: Include the egg wash and define six pastries from a measured dough and filling.
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Finely dice the onion and mix with the lamb, cumin, salt and pepper.
Roll out the pastry and cut into 6 equal squares. Divide the filling between them.
Fold into triangles and press the edges firmly to seal. Place on a lined baking tray.
Brush with the measured egg wash and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden and the filling is cooked through. Serve 2 pastries per portion.

name: Zwiebelkuchen
reason: Include butter and define the prepared dough, onion and egg mixture.
steps: Cover the prepared dough and leave to rise for about 1 hour, or follow its packet instructions.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the onions. Melt the butter in a pan and soften the onions for 20–25 minutes. Cook the diced bacon with them and let the mixture cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Roll out the dough to line a 20 × 25 cm baking tray.
Whisk the eggs, sour cream, salt and caraway seeds. Stir in the cooled onion and bacon mixture and spread over the dough.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the filling is set and the base is cooked. Cut into 6 portions.

name: Currywurst
reason: Specify cooked sausage weight and include the sauce sugar and water.
ingredients: 3 g for sauce; 1 g for finishing
steps: Heat the fully cooked sausages in a non-stick pan or under a grill for 10–15 minutes, turning occasionally, until hot throughout.
Meanwhile, combine the ketchup, 3 g curry powder, paprika, Worcestershire sauce, sugar and water. Simmer gently for 3–5 minutes.
Slice the sausages onto 2 plates, spoon over the sauce and finish with the remaining curry powder. Extra fries or bread are optional and are not included in these quantities.
